record.what_it_does: A customizable work-management and CRM platform built from apps, items, tasks and workflows.
record.auth_notes: Every flow is OAuth2-based and starts from an API key (client_id and client_secret). The current docs list four flows. Server-side flow is OAuth2 authorization code and the preferred flow for web apps. Client-side flow is implicit. Username & password flow is a last resort, and the older page says it is for trusted clients only. App authentication uses an app_id plus an app token, works for a single Podio app, and does not act as a user. App authentication is listed as "other". The older doc page saying "Two step authorization is not yet completed!" is legacy text; the current /authentication page documents the server-side flow as preferred.
record.access_notes: The API is available on free and paid accounts at no extra charge within the base rate limits. The pricing page lists 1,000 calls/hour on Free, Plus and Premium. Only paid plans can buy add-ons for higher limits (2,500 to 50,000 calls/hour). Certain restricted operations, and programmatic access to app tokens, require contacting Podio support with a project description and the client_id. No app-review process for public OAuth distribution is documented. The free plan is capped at 100 items per organization.
record.api_breadth_notes: The docs describe "a complete programmable interface to all Podio functionality". It covers items, apps, spaces, orgs, tasks, comments, files, contacts, hooks, statuses and more, which is well over 50 operations. Operations were not counted exactly. Client libraries exist for several languages.
record.mcp_notes: https://mcp.podio.com/mcp is hosted by Progress (Podio's vendor). It uses OAuth, works with default credentials or your own API key's client ID and secret, and exposes 22 read/write tools. It is in beta, "intended for evaluation and testing".
record.blocker_notes:
Nothing major blocks a build. Minor caveats:
- Rate limits are modest at 1,000 calls/hour on base plans, and only paid plans can buy add-ons for more.
- A few restricted operations need a support request.
- The vendor MCP server is in beta.
- Some legacy doc pages are stale or return 410.

evidence.quote: The Podio API is a complete programmable interface to all Podio functionality.
This is the preferred way of authenticating for web apps.
Use app authentication if you only need to interact with a single Podio app
The Podio API is available to use for both paid and free Podio accounts.
Certain API operations are limited to API clients with an increased trust level.
Hooks are webhooks that can call external sites when certain actions occur in Podio.
The Podio MCP Server gives your AI assistant 22 tools covering both reading and writing your Podio data
The Podio MCP Server is currently in beta and is intended for evaluation and testing.

changes.why: developers.podio.com/authentication lists all four flows, including app authentication, which confirms the 'other' method.
